headline.injury_figures_note: The 16 August, 07:30 WIB Kemenkes report states (on its summary slide) Luka Ringan/Rawat Jalan (minor/outpatient) = 50 and Luka Berat/Rawat Inap (serious/inpatient) = 104. Its per-district table is headed 'MD LB LR PGS' but the column that sums to 50 appears where 'LB' is labelled and the column summing to 104 appears where 'LR' is labelled — the reverse pairing from the summary slide. This SitRep follows the summary slide's explicit labels (minor=50, serious=104) for headline figures, and flags this apparent table/label mismatch in the source document rather than silently resolving it. This report's totals (154 injured) also differ from the same day's BNPB figure (101 injured) and the previous 15 August Kemenkes report (113 injured, 36 serious/77 minor) — all three are preserved rather than combined.

heoc_status.formation: Kemenkes formed the Health Emergency Operation Center (HEOC) the night of 15 August, after the Minister of Health led a virtual (Zoom) coordination meeting with all NTT provincial and regency/city Dinas Kesehatan (Dinkes) heads, all RSUD directors in NTT, and all puskesmas heads across the 8 affected regencies/cities; an advance team was also sent from Jakarta to assess conditions on the ground.
heoc_status.structure_status: As of 16 August morning, Kemenkes' Health Crisis Center said the HEOC's detailed command structure was still being finalised.
heoc_status.needs_mapping_scope: Detailed identification of health problems, affected facilities, medical equipment and medicine needs, intended as a reference for volunteer teams (where to go, what is needed, who to contact).
heoc_status.cross_reference: Reported alongside, not confirmed identical to, the 'nine Health Emergency Operation Centres activated' at provincial and regency level already recorded in emergency_response above.

recovery_targets.puskesmas_severe_damage_discrepancy: Menkes Budi Gunadi Sadikin's 16 August verbal figure ('6 puskesmas rusak berat', dozens moderate, hundreds light) differs from the Health Crisis Center's tabulated 20 severely damaged / 37 moderately damaged / 11 lightly damaged puskesmas already used elsewhere in this SitRep (see facility_summary.puskesmas). Both are shown rather than reconciled, consistent with this SitRep's general approach to cross-statement discrepancies.
recovery_targets.dispatch_attribution_note: The 16 August ANTARA report quotes Agus Jamaludin (Kemenkes' Pusat Krisis Kesehatan) describing a dispatch of 8 basic medicine packages, 5 emergency kits, 1,000 sterile gloves, 20,000 non-sterile gloves, 20,000 surgical masks, 10 oxygen concentrators and 2 health-post tents (plus 8 more on standby for a Type-1 fixed EMT) as his own centre's shipment. This SitRep's planned_logistics section separately attributes an identical list to the NTT Provincial Health Office (Dinas Kesehatan Prov. NTT). This most likely reflects the same national-to-provincial dispatch described from two vantage points (sending agency vs. receiving/coordinating provincial office) rather than two separate shipments; it is not double-counted in this SitRep.
recovery_targets.ngada_facility_note: BPBD Ngada's Pusdalops recorded 14 health facilities affected in Ngada Regency alone (puskesmas, RSUD and posyandu combined — a broader mix than the puskesmas-only figures above), alongside 8 injuries (7 minor, 1 moderate), as of its 15 August, 19:00 WITA update. Puskesmas Maronggela (Kecamatan Riung Barat) was reported severely damaged and in need of an emergency tent — see facilities below.

data_quality_notes: The report gives a date but no specific data cut-off time.
The puskesmas building-condition categories total 184, six fewer than the stated total of 190; these six are recorded as unclassified rather than assumed to be undamaged.
A dash in a district casualty cell is treated as no casualty report in the source table, not automatically as a verified zero.

BNPB reported 18 affected health facilities at 17:00 WIB, while the Ministry of Health report lists structural damage at 77 facilities. These are shown separately because definitions and cut-offs differ.

The 16 August, 07:30 WIB Kemenkes V1 report's per-district injury table appears to have its 'LB' (serious) and 'LR' (minor) columns in the opposite order from the report's own summary-slide labels; see headline.injury_figures_note.

Several figures in the 16 August V1 report's per-district table carry an asterisk in the source document with no visible footnote legend in the pages reviewed; this SitRep reproduces the numeric values without being able to confirm what the asterisk denotes.
disclaimer: Ministry of Health figures remain the primary source for detailed health-sector status. BNPB's separate count of 18 affected health facilities at 17:00 WIB is retained for comparison and is not combined with the Ministry of Health's 77 structurally damaged facilities. All figures remain preliminary.

bnpb.previous_note: BNPB's own reported total rose from 18 (15 Aug, 17:00 WIB) to 211 (16 Aug, 21:00 WIB) as province-wide data collection continued.
bnpb.reading_correction_note: The 16 Aug 21:00 WIB infographic's breakdown was initially misread in this SitRep as '2 hospitals + 199 puskesmas'; on re-inspection at higher resolution, and confirmed by the 17 Aug 07:00 WIB infographic restating the identical 21/190 split, the correct breakdown is 21 hospitals + 190 puskesmas — which matches the Ministry of Health's own province-wide facility baseline (21 hospitals, 190 puskesmas) exactly. This resolves the apparent 'puskesmas affected exceeds puskesmas that exist' inconsistency flagged in the previous pass.

cross_source_comparison.interpretation: Do not subtract or combine the figures. BNPB reports affected health facilities on its own, broader definition — 211 (21 hospitals + 190 puskesmas), unchanged between BNPB's 16 Aug 21:00 WIB and 17 Aug 07:00 WIB infographics — while the Ministry of Health reports facilities specifically classified with structural damage (77: 9 hospitals + 68 puskesmas, see facility_summary above). BNPB's 21/190 breakdown exactly matches the total number of hospitals and puskesmas in the Ministry of Health's own province-wide baseline below, which suggests BNPB is counting essentially every health facility in the affected area as 'terdampak' (affected, in some way) — a much broader threshold than the Ministry of Health's 'structural damage' classification. Source, source table and cut-off all differ; this SitRep flags rather than resolves the gap.
